title: Derived extension from one level of a varying-coefficient system
statement:
Let $\mathcal T=\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ for a small site $\mathcal C$. Let $O$ be a commutative ring and $\lambda\in O$ a non-zero-divisor such that $O\cong\varprojlim_{n\geq1}O/(\lambda^n)$, and set $A_n=O/(\lambda^n)$. Write $\mathsf S_A(\mathcal T)$ for the category of systems of sheaves of $(A_q)_{\mathcal T}$-modules $M_q$, with transition maps $M_{q+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{A_{q+1}\to A_q}M_q$ linear over $(A_{q+1})_{\mathcal T}$ and compatible componentwise morphisms [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Kernels and cokernels are componentwise. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $n\geq1$, let $e_n$ be evaluation at level $n$, which is exact.

Define $E_n:\operatorname{Mod}((A_n)_{\mathcal T})\to\mathsf S_A(\mathcal T)$ by
$$ (E_nF)_q=\begin{cases}F\otimes_{A_n} A_q&q\leq n,\\0&q>n,\end{cases} $$
with quotient-induced transitions, and by tensoring morphisms with the identity [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then $E_n\dashv e_n$. Its total left derived functor $LE_n$ exists and is left adjoint to the termwise derived evaluation $e_n$:
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathsf S_A(\mathcal T))}(LE_nN,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal T,A_n)}(N,e_nM),$$
naturally in both arguments. For a K-flat resolution $P\to N$ with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, lem-pc-kflat-resolution], the strict complex of systems $E_nP$ represents $LE_nN$; its differentials and maps are the displayed termwise tensors. Thus $e_qLE_nN\cong N\otimes^L_{A_n}A_q$ for $q\leq n$ and is zero for $q>n$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

For $m\geq n$ put $C_{mn}=-\otimes^L_{A_m}A_n$. There is a canonical natural map $\sigma_{mn}:LE_nC_{mn}\to LE_m$. On one flat-term K-flat representative $P$ over $A_m$, its components are the identity of $P\otimes_{A_m}A_q$ for $q\leq n$, after the canonical tensor associators, and the zero maps for $q>n$. These maps respect identity and composition of indices. For a derived system $M$, let $t^M_{mn}:C_{mn}e_mM\to e_nM$ be the adjunct, under the derived tensor/restriction adjunction [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors], of its transition $e_mM\to\operatorname{Res}_{A_m\to A_n}e_nM$. Under the displayed Hom adjunctions, precomposition with $\sigma_{mn,N}$ sends $h:N\to e_mM$ to $t^M_{mn}\circ C_{mn}(h):C_{mn}N\to e_nM$.

proof.text: Put $B_q=(A_q)_{\mathcal T}$, with its quotient ring maps. These are sheaves of commutative rings on the same small site. The strict semilinear system category $\mathscr S(B)$ of [lem-pur-system-level-left-extension] is exactly $\mathsf S_A(\mathcal T)$: its objects, morphisms and scalar restrictions are the ones specified in the statement. That node gives an abelian category, componentwise cohomology, exact evaluations and joint detection of isomorphisms. In particular a chain map of systems is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when every evaluated map is one, since its cohomology maps are evaluated componentwise. This applies to all unbounded complexes; there is no normalization condition.

proof.text: For $q\le n$ apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] to the identity topos and $B_n\to B_q$. Given $h:F\to M_n$, define the $q$th component $F\otimes_{B_n}B_q\to M_q$ by $x\otimes a\mapsto a\,\tau_{nq}^M(h(x))$, where $\tau_{nq}^M:M_n\to\operatorname{Res}_{nq}M_q$ is the iterated transition. Above $n$ use the unique map from zero. These maps are balanced and commute with restrictions, hence define sheaf morphisms. Their transition squares commute because the two paths send $x\otimes a$ to the reduction of $a$ times $\tau_{nq}^M h(x)$. Conversely a system morphism $E_nF\to M$ is forced to have precisely these components by its component at $n$, using $F\otimes_{B_n}B_n\cong F$. Thus evaluation at $n$ and this construction are mutually inverse natural Hom bijections. This proves $E_n\dashv e_n$, including the given action on maps. Its unit is $F\to(E_nF)_n$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, and its counit at $q\le n$ is the tensor-adjoint of $\tau_{nq}^M$, with zero source above $n$.

proof.text: Apply $E_n$ termwise to complexes. It is additive, so it preserves chain homotopies, shifts and the cone formula: the cone has entries $L^r\oplus K^{r+1}$ and a matrix differential, and an additive functor preserves that direct sum and each matrix entry. Consequently the functor $F_n:K(B_n)\to D(\mathsf S_A(\mathcal T))$, $P\mapsto Q(E_nP)$, is exact. Take the resolving class $\mathcal P_n$ to be the flat-term K-flat complexes. Every complex has a resolution from this class by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. For a quasi-isomorphism $s:P\to P'$ between its objects, [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings](1) makes $s\otimes1_{B_q}$ a quasi-isomorphism for every $q\le n$; above $n$ the map is $0\to0$. Step 1 therefore makes $E_ns$ a quasi-isomorphism of systems. All hypotheses of [lem-pur-left-derived-from-kflat-class] hold. It gives the everywhere-defined total left derived functor $LE_n$, with canonical comparison $LE_n(QP)\cong Q(E_nP)$ on $\mathcal P_n$. For a resolution $P\to N$, invert its derived image to obtain $LE_nN\cong Q(E_nP)$. The comparison is natural, so the displayed tensor maps and differentials compute the functor on these representatives. Finally [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings](2) identifies its $q$th component with $N\otimes^L_{B_n}B_q$ for $q\le n$; components above $n$ are zero.

proof.text:
Exact evaluation has the termwise derived functor by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]; [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] identifies this with its everywhere-defined right derived functor, so the ind-system of $e_n$ at every complex $K$ has the invertible identity-stage comparison $p_{\mathrm{id}}:Q(e_nK)\to Re_n(QK)$. For $E_n$, the quasi-isomorphisms of $K(B_n)$ form a saturated multiplicative system by [lem-pur-quasi-isos-saturated-triangulated], and step 3 verified that every complex has a resolution in $\mathcal P_n$ and that $QE_n$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms inside $\mathcal P_n$. Hence [lem-pur-resolving-class-essential-constancy] makes the pro-system $(QE_nP')_{P'\to N}$ essentially constant at every complex $N$, with invertible identity leg $u_{\mathrm{id}}:LE_n(QP)\to QE_nP$ when $P\in\mathcal P_n$; by [lem-pur-left-derived-defined-pointwise-kan-bridge] this cone is a pointwise right Kan extension, so its value and identity leg are the $LE_n$ and comparison of step 3. Apply [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors] to the adjunction of step 2 and these everywhere-defined derived functors. This gives the required unbounded Hom adjunction, natural in both derived arguments. Its bijection is the canonical one of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general], characterized by $e(p_s\circ Q(f)\circ Q(t)^{-1})=Q(s)^{-1}\circ Q(a_h(f))\circ u_t$, where $a_h$ is the termwise homotopy adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] induced by step 2. Take a flat-term K-flat $P$, $t=\mathrm{id}_P$, $s=\mathrm{id}_{E_nP}$ and $f=\eta_P:P\to e_nE_nP$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$. Since $a_h(\eta_P)=\mathrm{id}_{E_nP}$, the formula sends $p_{\mathrm{id}}\circ Q(\eta_P)$ to $u_{\mathrm{id}}$. Thus, after identifying $LE_n(QP)$ with $QE_nP$ by $u_{\mathrm{id}}$, the derived unit $\eta^n_{QP}$ is represented by $P\to P\otimes_{B_n}B_n$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$; naturality of the bijection transports this along any resolution $P\to N$. More generally, for a chain map $g:P\to e_nK$ the transpose of $Q(g)$ is represented by the strict system map $E_nP\to K$ which step 2 assigns to $g$. Taking for $g$ a K-flat resolution $P\to K_n$, with $t=g$, gives the derived counit at $QK$ as the system map corresponding to $P\to K_n$, precomposed with $u_g$. This verifies the asserted normalization.

For later use apply [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] to the identity site and the quotient map $B_m\to B_n$, with $R_{mn}=\operatorname{Res}_{B_m\to B_n}$ applied termwise. It gives $C_{mn}\dashv R_{mn}$ on the unbounded categories. On a flat-term K-flat $P$ over $B_m$, its unit is represented by the ordinary coefficient map $P\to R_{mn}(P\otimes_{B_m}B_n)$, $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ (clause (1)). If $H$ is a complex over $B_n$ and $g:P\to R_{mn}H$ a chain map, the transpose of $Q(g)$ is represented by $P\otimes_{B_m}B_n\to H$, $x\otimes a\mapsto a\,g(x)$ (clause (2)); for a resolution $g=s$ this is the derived counit. These fix the coefficient-unit normalization used below.

proof.text:
Write $\tau_{mn}:e_m\to R_{mn}e_n$ for the natural transformation induced by iterated strict transitions; it descends to the derived categories since both functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Define $d_N:C_{mn}N\to e_nLE_mN$ to be the $C_{mn}\dashv R_{mn}$-transpose of
$$N\xrightarrow{\eta^m_N}e_mLE_mN\xrightarrow{\tau_{mn,LE_mN}}R_{mn}e_nLE_mN.$$
Define $\sigma_{mn,N}:LE_nC_{mn}N\to LE_mN$ to be the $LE_n\dashv e_n$-transpose of $d_N$. Both adjunction bijections are natural by step 4, so this defines a natural transformation on the derived categories, rather than a choice of maps between individual evaluations.

To compute it choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P$ over $B_m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], applied to the identity topos and $B_m\to B_n$, $P\otimes_{B_m}B_n$ is flat-term K-flat over $B_n$. Thus step 3 simultaneously represents the source by $E_n(P\otimes_{B_m}B_n)$ and the target by $E_mP$. The composite whose transpose defines $d_N$ is the quotient map $P\to R_{mn}(P\otimes_{B_m}B_n)$, by the unit computation in step 4 and the transition of $E_mP$. Its coefficient transpose is the identity of $P\otimes_{B_m}B_n$, by clause (2) of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] as recorded in step 4. By the representative-transpose formula of step 4 ([lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general], with identity denominators on the flat-term K-flat $P\otimes_{B_m}B_n$), the $LE_n\dashv e_n$ transpose is the strict system map of step 2, which therefore has component, for $q\le n$,
$$(P\otimes_{B_m}B_n)\otimes_{B_n}B_q\longrightarrow P\otimes_{B_m}B_q,\qquad (x\otimes a)\otimes b\longmapsto x\otimes\overline a b.$$
This is the canonical tensor associator; for $q>n$ the source is zero and its component is zero. It is a map of strict system complexes: below $n$ the square is coefficient reduction of this same formula, at the boundary the source transition comes from zero, and above it both source components are zero. Tensor associativity here is the explicit balanced map displayed above and its inverse $x\otimes b\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes b$; the sheaf tensor definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] makes these inverse formulas sheaf morphisms. Hence the computation includes differentials, maps and the asserted system transitions.

proof.text:
Check the index identities on the same representatives. If $m=n$, the source and target in step 5 are $E_mP$ after the unit tensor identifications and every nonzero component is the identity, so $\sigma_{mm}=1$. For $l\ge m\ge n$ choose a flat-term K-flat $P$ over $B_l$. Repeated use of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] shows that $P\otimes_{B_l}B_m$ and its scalar extension to $B_n$ compute the successive derived coefficient changes. The balanced tensor associator identifies $C_{mn}C_{lm}N$ with $C_{ln}N$: on representatives its map is $(x\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes\overline a b$, with inverse given by inserting $1$. At $q\le n$, both the composite
$$LE_nC_{mn}C_{lm}N\xrightarrow{\sigma_{mn,C_{lm}N}}LE_mC_{lm}N\xrightarrow{\sigma_{lm,N}}LE_lN$$
and $\sigma_{ln,N}$ agree after the displayed coefficient associator. Explicitly, on a local generator $((x\otimes a)\otimes b)\otimes c$ of the source at level $q$, with $a\in B_m$, $b\in B_n$ and $c\in B_q$, the composite sends it first to $(x\otimes a)\otimes\overline b c$ and then to $x\otimes\overline a\,\overline b c$. The direct map first combines $a,b$ to $\overline a b$ in $B_n$ and then gives $x\otimes\overline a\,\overline b c$ in $P\otimes_{B_l}B_q$ as well. Here each bar denotes the specified ring map into the ring where that product is taken. At $q>n$ both maps have zero source. Thus they agree as actual strict system chain maps. For a fourth ring and a further coefficient $d$, every iterated associator sends $(((x\otimes a)\otimes b)\otimes c)\otimes d$ to $x\otimes\overline a\,\overline b\,\overline c d$; this proves associator coherence on generators, and hence on the sheafified tensors. Inserting $1$ gives the unit identities. Naturality and resolution independence from steps 3 and 5 make these identities hold on the derived functors. No flatness of any quotient $B_m\to B_n$ was used.

proof.text:
Let $f:LE_mN\to M$ have adjunct $h=e_m(f)\eta^m_N:N\to e_mM$. By the definitions of $\sigma$ and $d$ in step 5, the $LE_n\dashv e_n$-adjunct of $f\sigma_{mn,N}$ is $e_n(f)d_N$. Transposing this under $C_{mn}\dashv R_{mn}$ gives
$$R_{mn}e_n(f)\,\tau_{mn,LE_mN}\,\eta^m_N
 =\tau_{mn,M}\,e_m(f)\,\eta^m_N
 =\tau_{mn,M}h,$$
where the first equality is the naturality square of $\tau_{mn}$ for the derived morphism $f$. Conversely, by naturality of the coefficient adjunction $C_{mn}\dashv R_{mn}$ of step 4 [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction], the coefficient-adjunct of $\tau_{mn,M}h$ is $t^M_{mn}\,C_{mn}(h)$, directly from naturality of that adjunction's Hom bijection, with $t^M_{mn}$ the adjunct of $\tau_{mn,M}$ as in the statement. This proves the required precomposition formula for every derived system $M$ and every derived map $h$, including morphisms not represented by a single strict map. It also proves its naturality in both variables. All identities in this step are substitutions into the adjunctions already constructed and the naturality square just displayed.
